title: The Borrowed Umbrella
text:
Lucía found the umbrella on a bench outside the old library. It had a faded red handle and a name written inside, but the name had been scratched away. For three days she carried it to school, hoping its owner would come looking for it.

On the fourth day, an elderly man approached her at the bus stop and asked, without much hope, whether she had seen an umbrella. Lucía handed it over, and he smiled as though he had recovered something far more valuable. He explained that his late wife had bought it decades ago. Lucía walked home thinking about how small objects can carry memories.

questions.text: Where did Lucía find the umbrella?
options: On a bench outside the old library

questions.text: What did the elderly man explain about the umbrella?
options: He had bought it the day before
A friend had lent it to him
His late wife had bought it decades ago
It was a gift from Lucía

questions.text: Why did the elderly man smile when he received the umbrella?
options: He was amused by Lucía's story
He thought the umbrella was worth a lot of money
The umbrella meant more to him than its practical value
He had expected to lose it forever

questions.text: What does Lucía's final thought suggest about her?
options: She is indifferent to other people's feelings
She regrets helping the old man
She is reflective and values emotional meaning
She plans to keep the umbrella

marked with thin, shallow cuts on a surface
came near to someone or something
got back something that had been lost

paragraph_translations: Lucía encontró el paraguas en un banco frente a la vieja biblioteca. Tenía un mango rojo descolorido y un nombre escrito en el interior, pero el nombre había sido rayado. Durante tres días lo llevó a la escuela, con la esperanza de que su dueño viniera a buscarlo.

Al cuarto día, un hombre mayor se acercó a ella en la parada del autobús y le preguntó, sin mucha esperanza, si había visto un paraguas. Lucía se lo entregó, y él sonrió como si hubiera recuperado algo mucho más valioso. Explicó que su difunta esposa lo había comprado hacía décadas. Lucía regresó a casa pensando en cómo los objetos pequeños pueden guardar recuerdos.
